IS : 5425 ( Part 3 ) - 1987 

Indian Standard 

METHODS OF 
CHEMICAL ANALYSIS OF MISCH METAL 

PART 3 DETERMINATION OF IRON 

0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( Part 3 ) was adopted by the Indian Standards 
Institution on 16 January 1987, after the draft finalized by the Methods 
of Chemical Analysis of Non-Ferrous Metals Sectional Committee had 
been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 

0.2 Misch metal is an alloy of rare earth metals and is used for 
improving the strength, fluidity and other properties of cast iron, steel, 
aluminium, magnesium and nickel alloys to which it is added. Chemical 
analysis of misch metal is covered in parts. In this part, a method for 
determination of iron has been covered. Other parts are: 

Part 1 Determination of cerium 

Part 2 Determination of rare earths 

Part 4 Determination of aluminium 

Part 5 Determination of carbon 

0.3 In reporting the result of a test or analysis made in accordance with 
this standard, if the final value, observed or calculated, is to be rounded 
off, it shall be done in accordance with IS : 2-1960*. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard ( Part 3 ) covers the method for determination of iron 
in various grades of misch metal as specified in IS : 4182-19671". 

2. QUALITY OF REAGENTS 

2.1 Unless specified otherwise, analytical grade reagents and distilled 
water ( see IS : 1070-1977* ) shall be employed in the test. 



♦Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised ). 
fSpecification for misch metal. 

^Specification for water for general laboratory use ( second revision ). 

3 



IS : 5425 ( Part 3) - 1987 

3. DETERMINATION OF IRON BY SPECTROPHOTOMETRIC 
METHOD 

3.1 Outline of the Method — Iron is reduced with hydroxylamine- 
hydrochloride and treated with O-phenanthroline at pH 4'0. The red 
colour developed is measured at 510 nm against a reagent blank. 

3.2 Reagents 

3.2.1 Dilute Hydrochloric Acid— 1 : 1 ( v/v ). 

3.2.2 Hydroxylamine Hydrochloride — Dissolve 25 g of the reagent 
in 100 ml of water. 

3.2.3 O-Phenanthrolne — Dissolve 1 g of the reagent in one litre of 
water. 

3.2.4 Dilute Ammonia — 1 : 3 ( v/v ). 

3.2.5 Standard Iron Solution — Dissolve 0*500 g of cleaned electro- 
lytic iron wire ( Purity = 99*99 percent ) in 20 ml of dilute hydrochloric 
acid (1:1). Evaporate to dryness on a water bath. Add 1 ml of 
concentrated hydrochloric acid ( rd = 1*16 ) and water to dissolve it. 
Make up the volume to 500 ml. This solution is further diluted to give 
10 ^g of iron per ml. 

3.3 Procedure 

3.3.1 Weigh 2000 g of sample into a beaker. Add 50 ml of dilute 
hydrochloric acid to dissolve the sample and make up the volume to 
200 ml. 

3.3.2 In the case of Grade 2 ( high iron ) and Grade 3 ( lanthanum 
enriched ), take 5 ml of the sample solution from 3.3.1 and make up 
the volume to 100 ml. Take 10 ml each of the diluted solutions in the 
case of grades 2 and 3 and 10 ml aliquot from 3.3.1 in the case of 
Grade 1 sample in a 50-ml beaker. 

3.3.3 Add 10 ml of hydroxylamine hydrochloride and keep the beaker 
on a water bath for 10 minutes. 

3.3.4 Cool and and 2*5 ml of phenanthroline reagent. 

3.3.5 Add 10 ml water and adjust the pU to 4'0 by adding dilute 
ammonia ( avoiding precipitation of hydroxides ). 

3.3.6 Transfer the solution to 25-ml volumetric flask and make up the 
volume, 

3.3.7 Keep the solution for 30 minutes. Measure the absorbance at 
510 nm against a reagent blank obtained by starting with 1*0 ml of dilute 
hydrochloric acid and following 3,3.3 to 3.3.6. 



IS : 5425 ( Part 3 ) - 1987 

3.3.8 Take standard iron solution (10-100 ^g ) and develop the colour 
following 3.3,3 to 3.3.7, and plot the absorbance values against 
concentration of iron. 

3.4 Calculation 

Iron, percent = j^x in Grade 1 sample, or 

M 
= -=- in Grade 2 and Grade 3 samples. 

where 

M = mass of iron in pg obtained from the calibration graph.
